lines: Lorba Medical. Three clinics, one book.
A demonstration build of a primary care practice. Every patient and clinician here is invented.
Three neighbourhood clinics, run from a single appointment book.
A patient books in four short steps, starting with what the appointment is for.
Then where, and with whom. Choosing any location searches all three clinics at once, one book behind all of them.
The times offered are real availability, worked out from that same book. The patient picks one that suits them.
Details are filled in with sample data.
The booking is confirmed on the spot, with a reference, and labelled as simulated, because nothing is sent.
The front desk reads the same schedule. Not a copy, not a second system. The booking is already there.
Elsewhere in the day, a patient cancels.
The freed time goes straight to the waitlist.
Two of the three people waiting suit this time, each with its reason.
Reception offers it. The message is simulated.
The time is held, with a visible deadline.
The acceptance is simulated too, and the agenda updates the moment it lands.
The freed time is filled, and the cancellation stays on the board.
And one view covers all three clinics, worked out from the same records.
Occupancy, time held, and time still free.
